page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AMD EPYC 7R32 processors using the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 192 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store capacity. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core CPU performance in stress-ng is categorized in the bottom 10%, the multi-core CPU performance falls into the middle 50%. The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in specific workloads, achieving top 10% tier performance in PassMark CPU encryption tests, and top 25% performance in PassMark CPU score, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong, though large block read and write operations remain average. Redis SET operations also register in the top 25% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5ad.24xlarge offers a high density of physical cores and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, reducing the need for separate network-attached storage fees. However, the tradeoff lies in its lower single-core performance and lack of AVX-512 instruction support. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, cryptography, image processing, and database operations that benefit from local NVMe scratch space, rather than single-threaded or AVX-512 dependent vector calculations.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.24xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz. It includes 192 GB of DDR4 memory and 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, running on the Nitro hypervisor with 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate a tradeoff: single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core performance is average, and cryptography execution is in the top 10%. The instance also shows strong performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations. Qualitatively, the bundled local NVMe storage provides cost-efficient high-speed scratch space. This instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, cryptographic processing, and database operations requiring high-speed local storage.
